messages:
olivia_cust: Hey — after we upgraded to SDK v2 our function/tool calls to "ProcessData" started failing with 404 `tool not found`. This was working yesterday on v1.

olivia_cust: curl we send:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"tool_name":"ProcessData","args":{"id":123}}'
```

olivia_cust: response:
```
{"error":{"code":404,"message":"tool not found: ProcessData","suggestions":["check alias registry","try canonical tool id"]}}
```

maya_support: thanks — sorry about the break, looping in eng. Can you confirm SDK client version and whether you called via our JS SDK or directly to the REST API? Any special characters in the name?

olivia_cust: JS SDK v2.0.3 from npm, direct call via our server. No unusual chars we control, just PascalCase name.

liam_kapoor: looking. We shipped a change in SDK v2 that normalizes tool names before sending (to address historic alias collisions). It uses unicode casefolding; suspecting the normalization path is turning ProcessData -> processdata but our registry aliasing is sometimes indexed with mixed case.

liam_kapoor: can you paste response headers from the failing request? Especially `x-rw-registry-cache` / `x-rw-client-name` if present.

olivia_cust: headers attached from server logs:
```
x-rw-registry-cache: hit;ttl=96
x-rw-client-version: redwood-js/2.0.3
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
```

sanjay_shah: this smells like a case-normalization/alias-sync mismatch. Registry stores aliases in their original form and also a folded index for lookup. There was a migration last quarter that introduced casefold keys for certain unicode edge cases; some older aliases still have ASCII-lowercase keys. If the client uses full unicode casefold, the lookup may produce a different key than the registry index.

sanjay_shah: quick grep of registry logs around the time the alias was created shows:
```
[2025-11-02T18:23:11Z] alias_create: name="ProcessData" -> uuid=tool_abc123 index_key="ProcessData"
[2025-11-02T18:23:12Z] alias_index: key_lowercase="processdata" -> uuid=tool_abc123
```
But the index compaction job that writes the casefolded keys crashed during an earlier deploy and didn't run for a subset (region-eu).

devops-bot: deploy notified: redwood-sdk-js v2.0.3 released by @liam_kapoor at 2026-03-15T09:17:02Z

liam_kapoor: confirmed — SDK v2 defaults to Unicode casefolding to reduce collisions (e.g., Turkish dotted/dotless I). But our registry lookup currently expects ASCII lowercasing for backward compatibility. We're seeing a mismatch for aliases created before the casefold migration.

liam_kapoor: short repro on our side:
```
> python -c "import unicodedata; print('ProcessData'.casefold())"
processdata
```
vs registry lookup path which does `.lower()` for ascii only.

maya_support: customer needs a workaround ASAP — latency and retries are causing production errors for them. Any hotfix?

liam_kapoor: workaround options:
- client side: pass the canonical alias `processdata` (lowercase) instead of `ProcessData`, or set the SDK option `preserveAliasCase: true` (temporary flag in 2.0.4-beta).
- server side (short term): we can add a compatibility layer that checks both `.casefold()` and `.lower()` index keys when resolving aliases. Will push a patch to registry lookup service.

olivia_cust: trying the lowercase alias now...

olivia_cust: That fixed it. Calls succeed with `tool_abc123` and response is normal. Thanks.

sanjay_shah: long term we should standardize on a single normalization strategy and reindex aliases. Plan:
1) run full alias compaction job to populate casefold keys in all regions.
2) deploy registry lookup patch to check both keys for 48h (canary then full).
3) add telemetry to detect mismatched-lookups and emit metrics.

liam_kapoor: opened internal bug: RW-9521 (SDK-casefold-registry-mismatch). PR stub: https://internal.redwood/pull/9521 (will add tests).

maya_support: documenting workaround in the ticket and emailing the customer with steps (use lowercase alias or upgrade to 2.0.4-beta with `preserveAliasCase`). cc @olivia_cust — will follow up when fix is in prod. :thumbsup:

olivia_cust: Appreciate the quick help. Please ping when the reindex is done, we'd prefer not to keep using the workaround long-term.

liam_kapoor: noted — reindex scheduled for tomorrow 04:00 UTC, small blast radius. We'll post a follow-up in #eng-oncall after completion.

maya_support: closing this support thread for now since customer confirmed workaround. Will re-open if anything regresses.
